title: Unified incident attachment protocol for traces, metrics, and runbooks
creator: Ethan Monroe
description: Design and implement a small, consistent payload protocol and attachment pipeline so PagerDuty alerts and Slack incident threads carry a curated, size-limited bundle of artifacts: top spans (trace), condensed metric windows, selected log excerpts, and the exact runbook fragment used for remediation. Goals: reduce TTR, avoid noisy attachments, and make oncall handoff deterministic across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.
motivation: On several recent incidents, responders spent time hunting traces, recreating metric graphs, or guessing which runbook revision was applied. Attaching a compact artifact bundle to PD incidents and Slack threads will accelerate diagnosis and create repeatable evidence for postmortems.
technical_decisions: Use a JSON-LD style attachment schema (attachment_type + versioned payload) to allow future expansion without breaking older consumers
Generate attachments at the observability service edge (near ingestion) to avoid pulling large traces at incident time; use precomputed condensed views for last-5m/15m
Apply client-side redaction and a privacy filter pipeline step (PII rules from security team) before attaching to external channels
Limit attachment size to 128KB and fall back to a signed short-lived URL to S3 if payload exceeds limit
Attach a runbook fragment by ID + commit sha rather than full text when size-constrained; include an inline summary paragraph
tradeoffs: Precomputing condensed traces increases storage and compute near ingestion but drastically reduces time-to-build attachments during incidents
Using signed URLs keeps attachments verifiable and auditable but creates an operational dependency on object infra and presigned link expiry handling
Tighter size limits mean less context in-line; we accept a short redirect to a private store for full artifacts to preserve Slack/PagerDuty ergonomics
acceptance_criteria: PD incident payloads consistently include an 'redbox' artifact with trace top spans, metric snapshots, log excerpt, and runbook fragment when triggered by SLO alerts
Slack incident thread actions render the artifact as an interactive summary card with expand-to-view signed URL
Attachment pipeline applies PII redaction rules and logs a redaction audit event
End-to-end latency for generating an attachment at alert time is <3s for precomputed artifacts, <6s when composing on-demand with caches
Unit/integration tests and a migration doc for existing PD/Slack webhook consumers are merged
implementation_plan: Schema: define attachment JSON-LD spec and version it (spec doc in Confluence)
Edge compute: add 'artifact-sampler' microservice to observability ingestion path to store condensed traces/metrics
Hook integration: extend PD webhook bridge to include attachments; add Slack BlockKit renderer for artifact cards
Security: integrate redaction rules and KMS tagging for signed URLs
Backfill: run a one-time condense job for last 30d for high-signal services
E2E tests: smoke with staging PD instance and a test Slack workspace; load test artifact generation pipeline
deliverables: Migration checklist: confluence link in deliverables doc
